identity.name: Polyglycerol polyricinoleate (polyglycerol esters of polycondensed fatty acids from castor oil)
synonyms: Polyglycerol esters of polycondensed fatty acids from castor oil
Glycerin esters of condensed castor oil fatty acids
identity.chemical_class: Mixed polyglycerol esters of condensed castor-oil fatty acids (non-ionic emulsifier)

function.mechanism: Amphiphilic PGPR species reduce interfacial tension and stabilize water droplets in fat-continuous systems.
common_food_categories: Edible ices (proposed extension assessed by EFSA)
Emulsified sauces (MPL revision assessed by EFSA)

adi.basis: EFSA 2017 re-evaluation revised prior SCF ADI to 25 mg/kg bw/day; 2022 follow-up did not flag safety concern for proposed extension of use.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA concluded no genotoxicity/carcinogenicity concern in the assessed dataset and recommended tighter impurity/specification limits in the 2022 follow-up.

fda.cfr_citation: 21 CFR 172.854 (related: polyglycerol esters of fatty acids)
fda.notes: No explicit 'polyglycerol polyricinoleate' / 'polyricinoleate' listing was found in the current Title 21 full XML searched from ecfr.gov.

adi.basis: WHO JECFA database chemical record 3166 lists ADI 0-7.5 mg/kg bw, evaluation year 1973 (Meeting 17).

concerns.summary: A 2023 mouse study including PGPR reported increased epididymal fat, blood lipids, and inflammatory markers in colon/liver contexts; findings are mechanistic/animal and not yet a regulatory reversal.
EFSA 2022 follow-up recommended stricter control of undesirable impurities (e.g., toxic elements, glycidyl esters, 3-MCPD-related controls) in E476 specifications.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2017 reported no concern regarding genotoxicity or carcinogenicity for PGPR in the evaluated dataset.
Chronic/carcinogenicity and reproduction studies indexed in PubMed did not identify major adverse outcomes at tested conditions.
Human volunteer data (short-term, up to 10 g/day) reported no consistent adverse clinical chemistry findings.

populations: Children/toddlers (higher intake per kg body weight in additive exposure contexts)
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA 2017 states exposure estimates did not exceed the ADI of 25 mg/kg bw/day in assessed scenarios.

risk_assessment.rationale: Evidence supports a limited-risk classification: EFSA and JECFA provide ADI-based acceptance and EFSA follow-up found no safety concern for assessed use extension. Counterpoints are impurity-management caveats and a recent animal mechanistic signal that warrant continued monitoring.
key_factors: EFSA ADI 25 mg/kg bw/day with no exceedance in assessed scenarios
